rounds.text: Madhur Industries Ltd presents a fundamental case of value destruction that renders its low price-to-book ratio misleading. While the company trades at a discount to book value [E1] [E6], this is a direct consequence of its inability to generate profit, evidenced by a negative return on equity of -7% compared to the sector benchmark of 8.5% [E8]. The business is actively eroding shareholder capital, as shown by a return on assets of -7.11% against a positive sector benchmark of 3.65% [E7]. Investors are further penalized by a complete lack of dividend yield, meaning there is no income return to compensate for the underlying operational losses [E3]. Conceded: [E1] and [E6]. The negative P/E of -9.47x confirms that the company is currently failing to produce earnings, leaving the market capitalization of ₹ 2.34 Cr without a foundation of profitability [E2] [E5].
